{{Short description|None}}
[[File:Ajax puchar.JPG|thumbnail|300px|[[AFC Ajax|Ajax]]'s international trophies displayed in the club's museum. The Dutch club is one of five teams to have won UEFA's three main club competitions until 2021: European Cup/Champions League (4), Cup Winners' Cup (1) and UEFA Cup (1).]]
The [[UEFA|Union of European Football Associations]] (UEFA) is the [[sport governing body|governing body]] for [[association football]] in Europe. It organises four club competitions: the [[UEFA Champions League]] (formerly European Cup), the [[UEFA Europa League]] (formerly UEFA Cup), the [[UEFA Conference League]] (formerly UEFA Europa Conference League), and the [[UEFA Super Cup]]. UEFA was also responsible for the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] and the [[UEFA Intertoto Cup|Intertoto Cup]] until their discontinuation in 1999 and 2008, respectively. Together with the [[CONMEBOL|Confederación Sudamericana de Fútbol]] (CONMEBOL), it also organised the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]], which was last held in 2004, before its replacement by [[FIFA]]'s [[FIFA Club World Cup|Club World Cup]].

Spanish side [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] have won a record total of 26 titles in UEFA competitions, nine more than [[AC Milan]] (Italy). Before the establishment of the Conference League in 2021–22, the only team to have won every UEFA club competition was [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] (Italy).<ref>{{cite web|language=it|first=Paul |last=Saffer|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0252-0d04623c4c2f-62fb1e2d232c-1000--paris-sulle-orme-della-juventus/|title=Paris sulle orme della Juventus|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|date=10 April 2016}}</ref> They received [[The UEFA Plaque]] on 12 July 1988, in recognition of [[UEFA club competition records and statistics#List of teams to have won the main European club competitions|winning the then-three seasonal confederation trophies]] – the UEFA Cup in [[1977 UEFA Cup final|1977]], the Cup Winners' Cup in [[1984 European Cup Winners' Cup Final|1984]], and the European Cup in [[1985 European Cup Final|1985]], the first club to do so.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.lavanguardia.es/preview/1988/07/13/pagina-53/33040569/pdf.html|title=Sorteo de las competiciones europeas de fútbol: el Fram de Reykjavic, primer adversario del F.C. Barcelona en la Recopa|trans-title=Draw for the European football competitions: Reykjavic's Fram, first opponent of F.C. Barcelona in the Cup Winners' Cup.|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|format=PDF|page=53|date=13 July 1988|access-date=15 November 2009|language=es}}</ref> Juventus additionally won their first Super Cup in [[1984 European Super Cup|1984]], their first Intercontinental Cup in [[1985 Intercontinental Cup|1985]], and the Intertoto Cup in [[1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup#Finals|1999]].<ref name="UEFA Plaque">{{Cite news |url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/1997/maggio/24/Tutto_inizio_con_poesia_ga_0_9705246555.shtml |title=Tutto inizio' con un po' di poesia |date=24 May 1997 |work=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]] |access-date=1 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081004071731/http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/1997/maggio/24/Tutto_inizio_con_poesia_ga_0_9705246555.shtml |archive-date=4 October 2008 |url-status=live |language=it |trans-title=It all started with a little poetry|page=10}}</ref> Upon winning the [[2024–25 UEFA Conference League]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] became the first club to win all four major UEFA club competitions (Champions League, Europa League, Cup Winners' Cup, and Conference League).<ref name=chelsea>{{cite news|date=28 May 2025|title=Chelsea complete set of UEFA club trophies|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/news/0299-1dde1c08e79d-c3b67b51e270-1000--chelsea-complete-set-of-uefa-club-trophies/|access-date=29 May 2025|website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations}}</ref>

Spanish clubs have won the most titles (67), ahead of clubs from England (52) and Italy (50). Italy is the only country in European football history whose clubs won the three main competitions in the same season: in 1989–90, Milan retained the [[1989–90 European Cup|European Cup]], [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] won the [[1989–90 European Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]], and Juventus secured the [[1989–90 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]].<ref name="grandslam">{{Cite news |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=1989/overview/index.html |title=1989/90: Rijkaard seals Milan triumph |date=23 May 1990 |website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |access-date=30 May 2015 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150607104404/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=1989/overview/index.html |archive-date=7 June 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

While the [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]] is considered to be the predecessor of the UEFA Cup, it is not officially recognised by UEFA and therefore successes in this competition are not included in this list.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/kind=1/newsid=2571.html |title=UEFA Cup: All-time finals |date=30 June 2005 |website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080309094213/http://www.uefa.com/uefa/news/kind%3D1/newsid%3D2571.html |archive-date=9 March 2008 |url-status=dead |access-date=15 March 2008}}</ref> Also excluded are the unofficial [[1972 European Super Cup]], the FIFA Club World Cup, and the [[FIFA Intercontinental Cup]], the latter two being organised by the world's governing body.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.archive.uefa.com/competitions/supercup/history/index.html |title=UEFA Super Cup – History |website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|access-date=22 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100820032123/http://en.archive.uefa.com/competitions/supercup/history/index.html |archive-date=20 August 2010 }}</ref>

==Winners==
===By club===
[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] holds the record for the most titles overall with 26, followed by [[AC Milan|Milan]]'s 17 titles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/teams/50051--real-madrid/ |title=Real Madrid |website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|access-date=12 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/nationalassociations/teams/50058--milan/ |title=AC Milan |website=UEFA.com|publisher=Union of European Football Associations |access-date=12 June 2019}}</ref> Spanish teams hold the record for the most wins in the three out of four main UEFA club competitions: Real Madrid, with 15 European Cup/UEFA Champions League titles; [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], with 7 UEFA Cup/UEFA Europa League titles; and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], with 4 Cup Winners' Cup titles. Real Madrid have the most Super Cup wins (6), and also share the most Intercontinental Cup wins (3) with Milan. German clubs [[Hamburger SV]], [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] and [[VfB Stuttgart]], and Spanish club [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] are the record holders in the UEFA Intertoto Cup (two titles each).

Before the Conference League was established in 2021–22, [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] were the only teams to win all of UEFA's three main club competitions (European Cup/UEFA Champions League, Cup Winners' Cup, UEFA Cup/UEFA Europa League). Juventus additionally won the Super Cup, the Intertoto Cup and the Intercontinental Cup, making it the only team to win six different UEFA competitions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Which teams have won all the major UEFA club trophies? |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025d-0f5b873cb860-61d680b0f8bc-1000--who-has-won-a-clean-sweep/ |access-date=28 April 2022 |date=20 May 2020|publisher=Union of European Football Associations}}</ref> Upon winning the Conference League in 2025, Chelsea became the first club to win all four main UEFA club competitions.<ref name=chelsea/>

===By country===
Spanish clubs are the most successful in UEFA competitions, with a total of 67 titles, and hold the record for wins in the European Cup/UEFA Champions League (20), UEFA Super Cup (17), and UEFA Cup/UEFA Europa League (14).<ref name="uefa">{{cite news |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/finals/newsid=421025.html |title=Final facts and figures |date=9 March 2007 |website=UEFA.com |publisher=Union of European Football Associations|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512030341/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/finals/newsid=421025.html |archive-date=12 May 2008 |url-status=dead |access-date=12 May 2008 }}</ref> English clubs have won 52 titles, including a record eight wins in the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup and three in the UEFA Conference League. Italian clubs are third with 50 wins, and have the most victories in the Intercontinental Cup (7); they also have a distinction of being the only ones who have won the three main UEFA competitions in the same season (1989–90).<ref name="grandslam" />

The following table lists all the countries whose clubs have won at least one UEFA competition, and is updated as of the [[2026 UEFA Super Cup]] played on 12 August 2026.
